text: So I urge you, brothers and sisters, by the mercies of God, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God — this is your spiritual worship.

versions.text: So I urge you, brothers and sisters, by the mercies of God, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God — this is your true worship.
versions.explanation: λογικὴν λατρείαν means worship that is 'reasoned/rational' and hence 'spiritual' as opposed to merely ritual; 'true' shifts the sense toward authenticity rather than the rational/spiritual character of the service. A footnote could note the alternative rendering 'reasonable service.'

text: Do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you can discern what God's will is — what is good and pleasing and perfect.

For by the grace given to me I say to every one of you: do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has assigned to each of you.

versions.text: By the grace given to me I say to every one of you: do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has assigned to each of you.
versions.explanation: The connective γὰρ links this exhortation to verses 1-2 and is dropped; restoring 'For' keeps the argument's flow without harming oral rhythm.

text: For just as in one body we have many parts, and not all the parts have the same function,
so we, though many, are one body in Christ, and each of us belongs to all the others.
We have different gifts according to the grace given to us. If it is prophecy, prophesy in proportion to your faith;
if it is service, serve; if it is teaching, teach;
if it is encouragement, encourage; if it is giving, give generously; if it is leading, lead diligently; if it is showing mercy, do it cheerfully.
Let love be genuine. Hate what is evil; hold fast to what is good.
Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo one another in showing honor.
Never let your zeal grow slack; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord.

versions.text: Never let your zeal grow slack; keep your spirit aglow; serve the Lord.
versions.explanation: 'Aglow' is a somewhat dated idiom and softens ζέοντες ('boiling, fervent'). 'Be fervent in spirit' is clearer for reading aloud; a footnote could note that 'spirit' may refer to the Holy Spirit.

text: Rejoice in hope, endure in affliction, persevere in prayer.
Share with the saints in their needs; pursue hospitality.
Bless those who persecute you; bless them and do not curse them.
Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
Live in harmony with one another. Do not be arrogant, but associate with the lowly. Do not be wise in your own eyes.
Repay no one evil for evil. Give careful thought to what is honorable in the sight of everyone.

versions.text: Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is good in the sight of everyone.
versions.explanation: 'Take thought for what is good' reads awkwardly aloud; προνοούμενοι means to plan ahead or give careful thought, and καλά here carries the sense of what is publicly honorable or admirable.

text: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
Do not take revenge, dear friends, but leave room for God's wrath. For it is written: "Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says the Lord."
On the contrary: if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink. For in doing this you will heap burning coals on his head.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
